sections: 4.2.2.4, printed pp248-249: accepted symbol progression, EIEOS initialization, assigned lane seeds
4.2.7.2, printed pp361-364: Gen3 SKP parity and state trailer; footnote66 binds 8GT/s rules to Base3.1

findings: No blocking defect found in accepted-only held output: ready_o only permits replacement when output is empty or consumed; state and diagnostics remain stable through backpressure.

The RTL transposed polynomial masks and Python serial transmitted-bit transform are structurally distinct. Least-significant payload bits are processed first, seeds match all eight assigned lanes, EIEOS initializes after its complete record and SDS advances rather than reseeds.

Variable standard SKP lengths are checked for literal symbols, ending marker and zero padding. SKPs hold state, reconstruct the 23-bit trailer in transmitted byte order, and never load a received state.
Parity updates use scrambled DATA bits, reset at SDS and each standard SKP, and compare only when a SKP directly follows DATA. Parity mismatch latches lane_error without format fault or retraining.
Unseeded records and malformed metadata latch format_fault; only reset/flush recovers. Accepted EIEOS can reinitialize LFSR while sticky diagnostics remain observable.

Author oracle tests cover all assigned seeds, stalls, SKP sizes, back-to-back SKP indicator policy, data parity/state diagnostics and actual source mutations. I inspected the source but did not rerun or reparse their complete captured corpus.
scope: Read-only source and oracle review against cached primary-reference text. No HDL/native/test/formal/timing rerun, no full link/LTSSM, TS field/DC-balance decode, EDS adjacency or cohort ownership acceptance. Reset/flush implementation inspected; no claim of an independent midstream reset campaign.
